transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-18
Start: 16:30 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hale (Redwood AE), Evan Liu (Redwood SE), Karen Ito (Novum Legal), Rajesh Patel (Novum Procurement), Maya Chen (Novum InfoSec), Liam O'Rourke (Platform), Sana Ali (Eng)

Summary (auto): quick procurement/legal intake to accelerate pilot approval; technical walkthrough focused on KMS/bring-your-own-key, audit logs, and data residency; agreed next steps for MSA redlines and SOC2 artifacts; scheduling security deep dive.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'll kick off, i'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Evan from our security and infra team.
00:08 Rajesh: hey, thanks Jordan. i've got about 45 minutes. our aim today is to get aligned on the legal asks so we can push the pilot to procurement next week.
00:15 Karen: hi all, from legal side i'll flag DPA points and a few MSA clauses around indemnity and data residency.
00:20 Maya: and i'll be focused on keys, encryption, and auditability. we've got some strict requirements for bank data.
00:28 Evan: great, short agenda: MSA/DPA high level, KMS options (BYOK, HSM), SOC 2 evidence, and a quick note on hosting modes — hosted, dedicated, private vpc.
00:38 Liam: quick one — we will need the ability to pin model versions and have traceability for requests; is that part of the offering?
00:44 Jordan: yes, you can pin versions and we expose request-level tracing in the console and via audit logs, which is helpful for compliance.
00:52 Sana: is the trace tied to token-level data or just metadata?
00:55 Evan: it's metadata plus request/response hashes when enabled. we don't store PII unless you opt into retention; the DPA can be configured for minimal retention for the pilot.
01:10 Karen: on the MSA — indemnity cap, limitation of liability, and export controls. also DPA needs to specify data categories and subprocessing list.
01:22 Jordan: understood. we'll provide a DPA template and a subprocessor list, and we're open to reasonable indemnity language.
01:30 Rajesh: procurement wants a sample PO and an estimated monthly spend for a 6-month pilot with Dedicated capacity.
01:36 Jordan: i'll prepare a price addendum — i'll include token estimates, dedicated node hours, and an option for burst capacity.
01:45 Maya: can you explain KMS options again? our legal team insists on customer-managed keys or HSM.
01:51 Evan: sure — two primary options: 1) Redwood-managed KMS with envelope encryption and SOC controls, 2) Customer-managed keys — BYOK via your cloud KMS or an HSM gateway for our Private deployment. the private on-prem package supports HSMs and offline key storage.
02:10 Karen: BYOK will likely be required; can you support AWS KMS and external HSMs?
02:15 Evan: yes to AWS KMS; for external HSM you can run our Private runtime or we can integrate via an HSM gateway. there are some network egress considerations for hosted mode that we can document.
02:27 Maya: what about key rotation, access controls, and separation of duties? we need to ensure keys can't be exported by vendor ops.
02:34 Evan: keys under BYOK remain under your control; Redwood holds only the wrapped key metadata. rotation is supported via standard KMS APIs; we also offer an HSM-backed flow where keys never leave the HSM.
02:48 Sana: quick follow — how do you handle logs? we need detailed audit logs for model input/output requests and admin actions for 12 months.
02:57 Jordan: audit logs are available; retention is configurable. for enterprise we can push logs to your SIEM or S3 in your tenant.
03:10 Maya: will logs include full request/response or truncated?
03:14 Evan: by default it's metadata and hashes. full request/response can be retained if you opt in, but that'll be noted in the DPA and is something legal must approve.
03:27 Liam: data residency — we have obligations to keep certain datasets in EU and US regions. can we route by geography?
03:32 Evan: yes, smart routing supports region pinning per-tenant; Dedicated or Private makes that easier to guarantee.
03:40 Karen: export controls and cross-border transfer language will need to be explicit.
03:44 Jordan: agreed, we'll include region commitments and a clause for control plane operations.
03:50 Rajesh: procurement question — what is the SLA for Dedicated?
03:54 Evan: SLA for Dedicated is 99.9% uptime and latency SLOs in the contract; for mission-critical workloads we can discuss stronger terms with a support premium.
04:06 Rajesh: and breach notification timelines?
04:08 Jordan: standard is 72 hours for incidents and immediate notification for security incidents; we can align on timelines with legal.
04:20 Maya: one more technical — session keys and KV cache. we rely on KV cache for latency; is that persisted?
04:27 Evan: cache is ephemeral in hosted mode but can be persisted in Dedicated with controls. apologies if earlier demos called it K-V cash.
04:36 Karen: ha, that's okay.
04:40 Sana: pricing question — if we do a 6-month pilot with staging in a dedicated pool and then scale up, how is pricing modeled?
04:48 Jordan: pilot pricing usually has a reserved baseline plus usage. i'll present a model: reserved node/hour + per-token tail usage. we'll give two tiers: hosted pilot discount and a Dedicated reservation discount.
04:59 Rajesh: will there be a minimum commitment?
05:02 Jordan: for pilot we can do a reduced minimum; for Dedicated you'd lock in a commit for the reserved capacity period.
05:09 Maya: does Redwood offer SOC2 artifacts and pen test reports? procurement needs to see them.
05:13 Evan: yes, SOC2 Type II report and a summary of pentest findings — we can share redacted reports via secure link.
05:22 Karen: about subprocessing — can you provide a current subprocessor list and the locations of cloud providers used?
05:28 Jordan: yes, we'll send a current subprocessor list and region maps.
05:33 Sana: curious about model variants — if the vendor model is updated, can we freeze versions for the pilot?
05:38 Evan: yes, pinning model versions is supported; we also support rollbacks.
05:44 Rajesh: timeline — if legal gets the redline on Friday and procurement fast-tracks, could we be in pilot by 2027-06-01?
05:52 Jordan: that's feasible pending legal and PO. we should target next steps to make that date.
06:00 Karen: one redline preference — limitation of liability needs to reflect banking risk appetite. can you accept carveouts for willful misconduct?
06:08 Jordan: we can take that back; typical carveouts for gross negligence are standard and we can discuss specific language.
06:16 Maya: auditability — we need immutable logs and tamper-evidence, do you support WORM storage or signed logs?
06:25 Evan: we can ship logs to your WORM S3 bucket or support signed append-only logs; we'll include implementation options.
06:34 Liam: curious about certificate management for mutual TLS between our VPC and Redwood private endpoints.
06:40 Evan: mTLS is supported for Private and Dedicated endpoints; certificates can be managed on your side or via our cert provisioning with strict rotation policies.
06:50 Rajesh: procurement will need bank-specific contract language around audit rights and regulatory notices.
06:56 Jordan: we'll prepare a procurement addendum template that includes audit windows and notice requirements.
07:05 Karen: also want to confirm retention and deletion process if we terminate — data return and secure deletion.
07:11 Evan: yes, data return/export APIs exist, plus cryptographic erasure for keys under BYOK; we'll document the deletion workflow in the DPA.
07:23 Sana: i've got a technical gotcha — latency matters for real-time fraud scoring, can Dedicated meet our 50ms p95 target for single-token steps?
07:31 Evan: we have latency profiles; for small-context fraud models Dedicated with optimized kernels and prewarmed KV cache should meet sub-50ms p95; we'll run a benchmark during pilot.
07:45 Maya: can you agree to support an on-site assessment if needed? some of our older controls require that.
07:51 Jordan: for enterprise customers we can schedule a controlled on-site assessment; we'll coordinate logistics.
07:59 Karen: ok that's helpful. in terms of immediate asks — we want the MSA redline, DPA, SOC2, subprocessor list, and a pricing addendum.
08:09 Jordan: understood. we'll get those artifacts to you — Evan will upload the security docs.
08:14 Rajesh: procurement also needs a form PO and billing contact. i'll send a template after this call.
08:21 Jordan: great. any more questions?
08:24 Maya: none from me.
08:26 Liam: all good.
08:28 Jordan: recap and next steps — Jordan to send MSA redline and price addendum; Evan to share SOC2 and KMS integration docs; Novum to provide MRQ and PO timeline. security deep dive scheduled week of 2027-05-24.
08:44 Karen: thanks everyone.
08:47 Jordan: thanks, talk soon.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions present (e.g., K-V cash vs KV cache), speaker overlaps, and shortened sentence fragments.

End of transcript.
